findings.claim: The assessment bases multiple UAR-specific findings on paths that are not present in the packet's file tree, making those codebase claims unsupported for downstream planning.
findings.evidence: The artifact cites `src/uar/a2ui/protocol.rs`, `src/uar/a2ui/presentation_selection.rs`, and `src/uar/runtime/manager.rs` in F2-F4, but `cited_paths` marks all three as `MISSING`; the file tree only shows a top-level `uar/agents` entry and does not list `uar/src/...`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either supply the referenced UAR source as part of the packet/reference context or rewrite these findings as explicitly external/reported claims that cannot be treated as verified repository evidence.

findings.claim: The assessment recommends changing PEM and releasing npm packages even though the packet does not establish PEM as a writable project dependency or include its source/release files.
findings.evidence: Goals say PEM is at `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/prometheus-entity-management`, but the project constraints state reference workspace folders are read-only and the file tree does not contain `prometheus-entity-management`; additionally, `cited_paths` marks `RELEASING.md`, `src/official/catalog.ts`, and `src/official/runtime.ts` as `MISSING`, while F10-F11 rely on them.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate external PEM work into a dependency/prerequisite with its own writable repo and evidence, or limit this assessment to consuming a published PEM package available to this repo.

findings.claim: The assessment under-assesses the goal to leverage flint-forge because it gives only reported, unverified conclusions and no packet-supported evidence for whether the library can be used.
findings.evidence: Goal: `Leverage prometheus-entity-management... and the flint-forge libraries`; F13 is entirely `[REPORTED]`, says publication status is `unknown`, and includes `UNVERIFIED` component coverage, yet the options table dismisses `@flint/react` because it has an `Own dialect, needs the Flint gateway`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add verifiable evidence for flint-forge package availability, API shape, dependency requirements, and compatibility, or mark the leverage decision as unresolved for analysis.

findings.claim: The assessment does not fully assess the requested registry design because it identifies absence of a registry but does not map all current AG-UI event/artifact types that need renderer entries.
findings.evidence: Goal requires `a registry that maps each AG-UI event and artifact type to a renderer component`; F1 only says dispatch is a `switch` and tool-name `if` chain, while F2 names only `attempt_manifest` and `provider_event` and F5 names `agui.state.patch` and `agui.artifact`, leaving no inventory of the complete event/artifact type set to be mapped.
findings.suggested_fix: Inventory the existing AG-UI event names, artifact types, and current render paths, then identify which require registered renderers, hiding, or adapter handling.

findings.claim: The assessment labels live production behavior and npm/package measurements as verified without packet evidence to reproduce those claims.
findings.evidence: F2 claims `A live chat turn on https://know-me.tools streamed 2 agui.artifact events on 2026-10-09`; F8 claims npm versions and exports were verified; F10 claims measured PEM typecheck/test results, but none of these artifacts appear in the file tree or cited paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach the capture/logs/package manifests/test output as evidence, or downgrade these to reported/unverified so planning does not depend on unverifiable measurements.
